Early skin-to-skin contact and neonatal outcomes: a randomized trial

Abstract

Background: Skin-to-skin contact immediately after birth may improve neonatal outcomes, but trial evidence from low-income settings is limited.

Methods: We randomized 400 term newborns in Dhaka to immediate skin-to-skin contact or standard care.

Results: Hypothermia occurred in 6% versus 19% of newborns (risk ratio 0.32).

Conclusions: Immediate skin-to-skin contact sharply reduced neonatal hypothermia and should be routine care.

Keywords: hypothermia; newborn.
